messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 about 350 light‑years from Earth and is still forming inside a protoplanetary disk.  Its radius is roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (≈ 200,000 km), making it the biggest planet we’ve been able to measure directly.

> *Key facts*  
> • **Mass**: ≈ 10–15 M_J (just below the deuterium‑burning limit that separates planets from brown dwarfs).  
> • **Radius**: ≈ 2.5–3 R_J.  
> • **Age**: Only a few million years old—still accreting material.  

Other very large exoplanets (e.g., HD 106906 b, 2M1207 b) have comparable masses, but HD 100546 b remains the most massive planet that has been directly imaged and whose size has been measured. If future observations discover a planet larger than this, it would become the new record holder.
